findings.issue: `IsUnital.tendsto_cons` assumes global unitality but uses it only at the single pseudojet `a`. This matters for the schemes the PR defers: a scheme that rescales a merged pair to be massless is unital at massless `a` only, so the global hypothesis blocks exactly the intended consumers — the same reason `IsCollinearExactOn` exists.

findings.issue: `IsCollinearExact.isCollinearSafe_iff`, the file's only safety transfer, requires exactness on all of `V`, so nothing consumes `IsCollinearExactOn`; by the PR's own account the `p` and `E₀` schemes are exact only on the massless momenta and will have to restate this lemma rather than reuse it.

summary: The set-restricted criterion bundles two implications whose hypotheses are each unused in the other direction, and the unitality results carry a hypothesis and a typeclass stronger than their proofs use. The set-restricted exactness notion also has no safety consumer, so the only safety theorem is inapplicable to the schemes that motivated it.
